# Item export
Export item records as a CSV file for spreadsheet users.

## Example
python3 export.py --input data/items.json --output build/items.csv

## Options
--input: JSON source file
--output: CSV destination file
--separator: column separator (default semicolon)

Runtime: Python 3.10+ standard library; no installation or network needed.

--- export.py ---
import argparse
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path
def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("source")
    p.add_argument("--dest", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--delimiter", default=",")
    args = p.parse_args()
    rows = json.loads(Path(args.source).read_text())
    target = Path(args.dest)
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with target.open("w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter=args.delimiter)
        writer.writerow(["id", "name"])
        writer.writerows((r["id"], r["name"]) for r in rows)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

+        self.names = ["coffee", "Tea", "juice", "teapot", "Tea", "TEA"]
+        self.original = self.names.copy()
+

def find(names, query, *, limit=None):
    """Return case-insensitive substring matches in input order, up to limit."""
    if limit is not None and limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be nonnegative")
    if limit == 0:
        return []

    needle = query.casefold()
    matches = []
    for name in names:
        if needle in name.casefold():
            matches.append(name)
            if limit is not None and len(matches) >= limit:
                break
    return matches

import unittest

from receipts import html_receipt, text_receipt


class ReceiptParityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty(self):
        self.assertEqual(text_receipt([]), "")
        self.assertEqual(html_receipt([]), "<ul></ul>")

    def test_order_quantities_and_cents(self):
        items = [("tea", 1, 20), ("cake", 2, -15), ("empty", 0, 0),
                 ("return", -1, -100)]
        self.assertEqual(
            text_receipt(items),
            "tea: 1 item @ 20c\ncake: 2 items @ -15c\n"
            "empty: 0 items @ 0c\nreturn: -1 items @ -100c",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            html_receipt(items),
            "<ul><li>tea: 1 item @ 20c</li><li>cake: 2 items @ -15c</li>"
            "<li>empty: 0 items @ 0c</li><li>return: -1 items @ -100c</li></ul>",
        )

    def test_escaping_and_whitespace(self):
        items = [(' <tea & "cake\'>\n&', 1, -2)]
        self.assertEqual(text_receipt(items), ' <tea & "cake\'>\n&: 1 item @ -2c')
        self.assertEqual(
            html_receipt(items),
            "<ul><li> <tea & "cake'>\n"
            "&amp;: 1 item @ -2c</li></ul>",
        )

    def test_singular_uses_equality_not_type(self):
        items = [("float", 1.0, 5), ("bool", True, 6), ("string", "1", 7)]
        self.assertEqual(
            text_receipt(items),
            "float: 1.0 item @ 5c\nbool: True item @ 6c\nstring: 1 items @ 7c",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            html_receipt(items),
            "<ul><li>float: 1.0 item @ 5c</li><li>bool: True item @ 6c</li>"
            "<li>string: 1 items @ 7c</li></ul>",
        )

    def test_single_pass_iterables(self):
        self.assertEqual(text_receipt(iter([("tea", 1, 20)])), "tea: 1 item @ 20c")
        self.assertEqual(
            html_receipt(iter([("tea", 1, 20)])),
            "<ul><li>tea: 1 item @ 20c</li></ul>",
        )
